title: Step Functions — concept map
intro: AWS Step Functions runs state machines defined in Amazon States Language (ASL). Each execution walks through states: Task invokes work, Choice branches on input, Parallel runs branches concurrently, Map iterates over arrays. Standard workflows are durable with full history; Express workflows are high-volume and cheaper per execution. Saga patterns use compensating transactions on failure. Lambda and SQS integrate as Task targets or worker patterns.

overviewDiagram.title: Step Functions execution flow
overviewDiagram.source:
flowchart TD
  START([Start]) --> T1[Task: validate order]
  T1 --> C{Choice\npayment OK?}
  C -->|yes| T2[Task: charge payment]
  C -->|no| FAIL([Fail state])
  T2 --> T3[Task: ship order]
  T3 --> END([Succeed])
  T2 -->|error| COMP[Task: refund\ncompensation]
  COMP --> FAIL

conceptCards.title: State types
conceptCards.summary: Task, Choice, Parallel, Map, Wait, Pass, Succeed, Fail. Task is 90% of production ASL.
conceptCards.example: Map over line items calling Lambda per item with MaxConcurrency

conceptCards.title: Standard vs Express
conceptCards.summary: Standard: durable, auditable, up to 1 year. Express: <5 min, high volume, lower cost.
conceptCards.example: Order saga = Standard; real-time auth check = Express

conceptCards.title: Saga pattern
conceptCards.summary: Forward steps with compensating rollback on failure. Step Functions Catch/Retry orchestrate.
conceptCards.example: Reserve → Charge → Ship; on ship fail → Refund → Release

conceptCards.title: Lambda + SQS
conceptCards.summary: Task invokes Lambda sync; or send to SQS and wait with callback token pattern.
conceptCards.example: Step Functions → SQS → worker Lambda → success/fail callback
